text.zh: 一男一女虽然并肩坐着，却各自封闭在沉默里，眼神空洞。
text.en: Though they sit side by side, the man and woman are each walled in their own silence, their eyes empty.

text.zh: 女子面前放着一杯浅绿色的苦艾酒。这幅画后来就因为它，被叫作《苦艾酒》。
text.en: In front of the woman is a glass of pale green absinthe. It later gave the painting the name by which it is known today.

text.zh: 这是巴黎皮加勒广场的“新雅典”咖啡馆，当时现代艺术家常在这里聚会。
text.en: This is the Nouvelle-Athènes café on the Place Pigalle in Paris, a meeting place for modern artists of the time.

text.zh: 德加请认识的人来扮演画中人物：女子是女演员艾伦·安德烈，男子是画家和版画家马塞兰·德布丹。
text.en: Degas asked people he knew to pose: the woman is the actress Ellen Andrée, the man the painter and engraver Marcellin Desboutin.

text.zh: 他们身后的大镜子里，映出了两人模糊的影子。
text.en: In the large mirror behind them, their shadowy silhouettes are reflected.

text.zh: 德加把签名“Degas”写在左下角报夹上的一张报纸上。
text.en: Degas signed his name on a newspaper on a newspaper holder, lower left.

exclusive._说明: 独家发现“镜子里的影子”：站到画家视角点时，画面放大到两人身后的镜子，显示卡片5的文字。只是放大原画，不是示意效果。crop 是镜子在原画上的位置（0–1），照着 images/absinthe.jpg 量的（上方一条，两个影子都在里面）。

title.zh: 第一幕 · 城市的画家

text.zh: 和他的印象派朋友们不同，德加喜欢画城市里的室内：剧院、咖啡馆，这些演出和休闲的地方。
text.en: Unlike his Impressionist friends, Degas was at heart a painter of the city, drawn to its interiors: theatres, cafés, places of entertainment and leisure.

alt.zh: 德加《苦艾酒（在咖啡馆里）》1875–1876，巴黎奥赛博物馆
alt.en: Edgar Degas, In a Café (The Absinthe), 1875–76, Musée d'Orsay, Paris

title.zh: 第二幕 · 画室里的咖啡馆

text.zh: 这幅画是在画室里画的，不是在咖啡馆里。人们常把它和左拉的小说《小酒店》联系在一起；左拉也对德加说过，他在书里不少地方，干脆就是描写了德加的画。
text.en: The painting was made in the studio, not in the café. It is often compared to Zola's novel *L'Assommoir*; Zola himself told Degas that in places he had simply described some of his paintings.

alt.zh: 德加《苦艾酒（在咖啡馆里）》1875–1876，巴黎奥赛博物馆
alt.en: Edgar Degas, In a Café (The Absinthe), 1875–76, Musée d'Orsay, Paris

title.zh: 第三幕 · 一个新名字

text.zh: 它原来的画名是《在咖啡馆里》，1876年在第二届印象派画展上展出。1893年在伦敦展出时，画名改成了《苦艾酒》。1911年，它进入法国国家收藏。
text.en: Its original title was *In a Café*, and it was shown at the second Impressionist exhibition in 1876. When it was exhibited in London in 1893, the title was changed to *L'Absinthe*. In 1911 it entered the French national collection.

final.en: Side by side, each alone in silence.
